artists.biography:
Matthew Charles "Matt" Berry (born 2 May 1974) is an English actor, writer, comedian and musician. Berry is perhaps best known for his appearances in The IT Crowd, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace, The Mighty Boosh, and Snuff Box. He is renowned for his deep voice; he has voiced several advertisements, most notably for Volvic, The Natural Confectionery Company, Absolute Radio, and MoneySupermarket.

As a musician, Berry composed all the music for Snuff Box, as well as the music for AD/BC: A Rock Opera, which he co-wrote with Richard Ayoade. AD/BC was a half-hour parody of overblown musicals in general and Jesus Christ Superstar in particular, telling the story of the innkeeper who allowed Mary, Joseph, and the baby Jesus to sleep in his manger. AD/BC was broadcast in December 2004 and featured Fulcher and Mighty Boosh stars Julian Barratt and Noel Fielding. He also performed a song for an episode of Garth Marenghi's Darkplace entitled "One Track Lover", a spoof of cheesy romantic 80s songs.

perplexity.description:
Matt Berry’s Night Terrors (Nocturnal Excursions In Music), released in 2017 on Acid Jazz, is an atmospheric and genre-blurring album that draws from jazz, folk, and experimental traditions. The record features eight tracks of moody, cinematic compositions, blending acoustic instrumentation with subtle electronic textures and Berry’s signature baritone vocals. Its sound evokes a nocturnal journey, with elements of acid jazz, pastoral folk, and avant-garde experimentation creating a dreamlike, introspective mood throughout.

Within Matt Berry’s discography, Night Terrors stands out as a departure from his more comedic and pop-oriented work, showcasing his versatility as a composer and performer. The album reflects his deep appreciation for British folk and jazz traditions, while also embracing a more abstract and immersive approach to songwriting. Released by Acid Jazz, a label known for championing eclectic and genre-defying artists, the record fits comfortably within their catalog of adventurous and boundary-pushing music.

Commercially and critically, Night Terrors (Nocturnal Excursions In Music) received modest attention upon its original 2017 release, appearing on niche genre charts but not achieving widespread mainstream recognition. Reviews highlighted its unique atmosphere and Berry’s skill in crafting evocative, otherworldly soundscapes, though it remains a lesser-known entry in his broader body of work.
